paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
model_annotation: This pie chart visually represents the distribution of samples across different levels of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and maximum ambiguity, arranged in two concentric rings. The chart displays a total of eight slices, with four representing standard deviation values in the outer ring and four representing maximum ambiguity values in the inner ring. In the outer ring, the slice labeled "Std: 0.0" is blue and occupies 49.0% of the circle, followed by "Std: 0.47" in a shade of purple at 38.0%, "Std: 0.82" in a lighter blue at 7.0%, and "Std: 0.94" in a pale green at 5.0%. The inner ring shows "Max: 1" in a muted purple representing 39.0%, "Max: 2" in a light blue at 47.7%, and "Max: 3" in a darker shade of blue at 14.2%. Percentage labels are provided for each slice, and a legend is included below the chart identifying the colors corresponding to the different standard deviation and maximum ambiguity values. The slices in both rings appear ordered roughly in descending size.
